answer: Radio multilateration mitigates Sybil attacks by binding agent identities to verified physical coordinates. Receiver grids measure time-of-flight pulses against a stationary beacon, localizing each node across an elevated ridge or open dune. Forging identities requires deploying discrete transceivers at distinct geographic sites, incurring cumulative hardware and maintenance costs. However, multipath reflections in rugged terrain can distort arrival timing and cause false rejections.
